debates.title: Weight‑space programming sparks safety concerns
debates.summary: New research shows frontier models can read and edit raw neural network weights, opening powerful new capabilities. The community is split between excitement over practical gains and alarm about recursive self‑improvement risks.

positions.stance: Highlights the paper that demonstrates GPT‑6 Astra and other frontier models can directly interpret model weights, calling it a breakthrough capability.
Reports an experiment where GPT‑6 Astra edited only 0.016% of a smaller model’s weights, boosting its math performance sixfold, showing immediate practical impact.
Warns that weight‑space programming removes autoresearch from the recursive self‑improvement loop, raising existential safety fears.

debates.title: Legal AI agents clash with data privacy
debates.summary: Legora’s lawyer‑focused AI agents can draft contracts and coordinate work, but the firm cannot inspect any of the agent’s actions because client data must stay private. This tension raises questions about testing, accountability, and regulatory compliance.

positions.stance: Describes how Legora builds agents that draft, edit, and review thousands of contracts for lawyers, showcasing the promise of AI‑augmented legal work.

debates.summary: A quote from Kyle Kingsbury notes that generative models make it easier to counterfeit documentation, threatening engineers’ confidence in software reliability. Maintainers are now asked to devise new verification methods to preserve quality and prove correctness.
